cards.title: Introduction to Validation in Flask
cards.content: Data validation is a critical step in web development. Never trust user input! In Flask, while you can manually check request data, using libraries like WTForms or Pydantic makes the process secure, robust, and maintainable.

cards.title: What is Flask-WTF?
cards.content:
Flask-WTF integrates WTForms with Flask, providing features like CSRF protection, secure form rendering, and built-in validators for email, length, data required, and more.

from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import StringField, PasswordField
from wtforms.validators import DataRequired, Email

class SignupForm(FlaskForm):
    email = StringField('Email', validators=[DataRequired(), Email()])
    password = PasswordField('Password', validators=[DataRequired()])

cards.title: Validating JSON APIs
cards.content:
When building REST APIs with Flask, requests usually come as JSON rather than HTML forms. You can validate incoming JSON payloads using libraries like Marshmallow or Pydantic.

from flask import request, jsonify

@app.route('/api/user', methods=['POST'])
def create_user():
    data = request.get_json()
    if not data or 'username' not in data:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Username is required'}), 400
    return jsonify({'success': True}), 201

cards.title: Validation Best Practices Summary
cards.content:
Always remember these key rules for robust validation in Flask:

  • Validate on the server side, even if client-side validation exists.
  • Always enable CSRF protection for HTML form submissions.
  • Sanitize inputs to prevent XSS and SQL injection attacks.
  • Use established libraries like Flask-WTF or Marshmallow instead of writing custom regex for everything.
